Fencing for Ruislip gardens

Many Ruislip homes have long, narrow back gardens with fences shared with neighbours on both sides, and often another boundary at the end of the garden. Over time, posts rot and panels lean or blow down. Replacing them properly gives you a straight, secure fence that lasts.

We offer:

  • New fencing for new boundaries and garden makeovers.
  • Fence replacement for old, rotten or leaning fences.
  • Storm-damage replacement to get your garden secure again [PLACEHOLDER: confirm you take on storm repair/replacement call-outs].

We will help you choose fencing that suits your garden and your budget [PLACEHOLDER: confirm fence types offered (panels, posts, gravel boards etc.)].

Local things to think about

  • Talk to your neighbours: With so many shared boundaries in Ruislip's semis and terraces, it is worth agreeing the plan with your neighbour before work starts, and checking your deeds for who owns which fence.
  • Height: A garden fence can usually be up to 2 metres without planning permission, or 1 metre next to a road or footpath [PLACEHOLDER: confirm planning wording]. Homes in Ruislip's conservation areas may have extra rules [PLACEHOLDER: confirm conservation-area wording].
  • Gardens backing onto woods and open space: Gardens near Ruislip Woods, Park Wood or the Lido can face more wind and wildlife, so a solidly built fence matters even more.
